bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Diesel Mechanic Salary in Australia

If you're researching the **diesel mechanic salary** in Australia, you'll find a wide range depending on whether you look at award minimums or actual market earnings. This article explains how to convert an hourly rate to annual pay using a 38-hour week, what the award says, what the ATO reports, and how tax and super affect take-home pay.

## Award Minimum Rates for Diesel Mechanics

Diesel mechanics are covered by the Vehicle Repair, Services and Retail Award (MA000089). The classification for a qualified tradesperson is Motor Mechanic (General) or Diesel Motor Mechanic under ANZSCO 321212. From 1 July 2026, the minimum hourly rate for a Tradesperson Level 1 (holding a Certificate III) is **$29.45 per hour**. For a 38-hour week, that works out to:

- Weekly: $29.45 × 38 = $1,119.10
- Annual: $1,119.10 × 52 = **$58,193.20**
- Fortnightly gross: $2,238.20

If you hold a Certificate IV qualification and use it in your role (Tradesperson Level 2), the rate is **$32.22 per hour**, equating to $63,669 per year. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate $36.81 per hour for Level 1.

A tool allowance of $13.86 per week applies if you supply your own hand tools. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and are the legal minimum.

## What Diesel Mechanics Actually Earn

Award rates are the floor. According to the Australian Taxation Office's 2023–24 taxation statistics, the median salary or wage for diesel motor mechanics was **$112,515**. That's significantly higher than the $73,505 median for general motor mechanics. Why the difference?

Jobs and Skills Australia reports that 93% of diesel motor mechanics work full-time, averaging **46 hours per week**. Many work in mining, heavy vehicle, or remote settings where enterprise agreements, overtime, and allowances lift pay well above the award. The median age is 32, and 72% hold a Certificate III or IV.

## Converting Hourly to Annual: The 38-Hour Week Assumption

When you see a salary figure based on an hourly rate, it typically assumes a standard 38-hour week and 52 weeks per year. The formula is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example:
- $29.45 × 38 × 52 = $58,193
- $32.22 × 38 × 52 = $63,669
- $50.00 × 38 × 52 = $98,800

This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work more than 38 hours, your actual annual pay will be higher. Use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and after-tax figures.

## Fortnightly Pay and Take-Home Tax

A fortnight is simply weekly pay multiplied by two. For the award minimum:
- Fortnightly gross: $1,119.10 × 2 = $2,238.20
- After income tax and Medicare levy (2026–27 rates): approximately **$1,891 per fortnight** 

Tax rates for 2026–27: nil up to $18,200, 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, 45% above. Medicare levy is generally 2%. The take-home estimate above uses these rates and the full tax-free threshold.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your base pay. For a diesel mechanic earning $58,193 per year, that's an extra $6,983 in super, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Super is not deducted from your hourly rate—it's an additional benefit. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

## Comparing Award Minimums to the National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). A qualified diesel mechanic's award rate of $29.45 is about 11% higher. Casual employees get $33.05 under the national minimum, but the award casual rate for a diesel mechanic is $36.81—so award coverage provides better conditions.

## Using the Timesheet for Your Own Rate

Whether you're negotiating a salary or checking an offer, you can convert any hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and after-tax figures using [the timesheet](/). Just enter your base hourly rate (do not include casual loading—use the checkbox to add 25% on top). The tool assumes a 38-hour week and 52 weeks, and estimates tax and super based on current rates.

For more on what different jobs pay, see [job pay](/topics/job-pay). If you're comparing award rates, check [pay guides](/blog) for the latest Fair Work Ombudsman schedules.

## Key Takeaways

- The minimum **diesel mechanic salary** under the award is $58,193 per year for a 38-hour week.
- Actual median earnings are much higher at $112,515, reflecting longer hours, overtime, and industry premiums.
- Always convert hourly rates using 38 hours × 52 weeks for a standard annual figure.
- Super is 12% on top, and tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates.
- Use [the timesheet](/) to personalise the calculation for your own rate and circumstances.
